writeup.1: The maker to start with works out of a unit on Broadhollow Road in Melville, New York. Jon Millman hand stamps, torches and paints copper discs under the name Golf Life Metals, and his own storefront sells replicas of the markers that won the 2025 and 2026 Masters, the 2025 Players, the 2025 Tour Championship and the 2021 Senior Open. The site says the work has been in play at the Olympics and the Ryder Cup, claims more than fifteen hundred designs for fifty-plus tour pros, and puts it plainly: back to back Masters won with GLM. Six inches down the same page sits a marker that says Fuck Bogeys.
writeup.2: The rest is a question of method. Seamus forges in Portland and Fyfe in Scotland, both striking metal by hand, so no two come out the same. Pins & Aces holds a real Coca-Cola licence and a second with a rolling-paper company. Matchstick draws its markers as illustrations rather than logos, which is how a dinosaur caddie and Chunk from The Goonies hold together at coin size. Sounder named two after a hill in Gloucestershire.
writeup.3: Seventy-seven markers from twenty brands sit in nine groups, running from hand-forged copper through licensed artwork to a line of drinks rendered in enamel. Prices go from six dollars to two hundred and fourteen, in five currencies, none of them converted, so every number is what the brand itself charges.
